# OpenClaw Skill Surfacing Plugin — PRD

## 1. Problem & Thesis

OpenClaw loads the entire installed skill library into every turn. The Roscoe profile carries 189 active skills. This is wrong on four axes at once:

- **Attention cost** — hundreds of skill descriptions burn context budget before the user's task is even read.
- **Selection accuracy** — the agent must route over a long, undifferentiated list; near-duplicate skills (PDF, GitHub, browser, research, legal) compete and the agent picks badly.
- **Isolation** — legal, coding, creative, ops, and social workflows are all equally "live," so domain instructions leak across unrelated work.
- **Trust** — every installed third-party skill body is in-context and can influence behavior even when irrelevant to the turn.

**Thesis:** Keep the full library *installed* but make surfacing a runtime decision. Per turn, expose a small (3–12) profile-authorized candidate set via hybrid retrieval; load full skill bodies only on explicit selection; log every decision. Ship it as a **plugin**, not a core rewrite, because the routing policy needs metrics-driven tuning before it earns default status.

The mental model the product must teach: **installed ≠ surfaced ≠ loaded.** Installed is inventory. Surfaced is a visible candidate card (metadata only). Loaded is the full `SKILL.md` injected into the active loop. These are three distinct states with three distinct gates. (`always_on` skills are a fourth, *pinned* sub-case of Loaded — see §3.)

## 2. Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**
- Cut always-visible skills from ~189 to a per-turn set of typically 3–12.
- Per-profile and per-workspace activation policy that is deterministic and testable.
- An agent-callable escape hatch (`skill_manifest_search`) for when ambient retrieval misses.
- Defer full-body loading until a skill is selected.
- Produce an audit record for every surface/load decision.
- Run fully local/offline by default; provider-backed embeddings optional later.

**Non-Goals**
- Replacing ClawHub (distribution/registry stays where it is).
- Changing the `SKILL.md` format.
- Auto-installing unknown third-party skills.
- Granting tools/permissions because a skill was retrieved or loaded. **Retrieval is not authorization. Loading is not authorization.** This is the load-bearing invariant of the whole design.
- A fine-tuned routing model in v1.
- Full programmatic conflict-resolution between simultaneously-loaded skill bodies (scoped to v1.5 — see §5.7).

## 3. The Three-State Model (normative)

| State | What it means | Gate to reach it | Cost |
|-------|---------------|------------------|------|
| Installed | Skill exists in a scanned root, indexed | indexer run | disk |
| Surfaced | Skill **card** (metadata, ~200 tokens) shown to agent for this turn | profile/workspace policy + retrieval score ≥ threshold | small per-turn |
| Loaded | Full `SKILL.md` body injected | explicit `skill_load` (agent or user) + policy re-check | full body tokens |
| Loaded · **pinned** (`always_on`) | Full `SKILL.md` body **auto-injected at session/profile init** | one-time policy/risk check when `skill-policy.yaml` is authored/loaded — **not** per-turn retrieval, **not** the per-turn `skill_load` gate | full body tokens, persistent |

The card is the unit of surfacing. It is generated, bounded, and never contains executable operational instructions — only enough to let the agent decide whether to load. This bound is what makes surfacing safe even for medium/high-risk skills.

**Pinned (`always_on`) skills** are the one path into the Loaded state that does not run per-turn. They are admitted once, by a one-time policy/risk check at the time the profile's `skill-policy.yaml` is authored or loaded, and their full bodies are then auto-injected at init. The agent never has to discover or manually load them. Being pre-loaded does **not** exempt them from the §5.7 security invariants: a pinned skill still cannot self-authorize tools, edit policy, or raise its own risk gate. Pinned skills are **infrastructure**, not surfaced candidates — they are counted against neither the default nor the hard cap, and they do **not** displace dynamic surfacing slots.

## 4. Skill Card

Generated per skill at index time:

```yaml
id: firmvault-case-context-from-wiki
name: FirmVault Case Context From Wiki
description: Load case-level context from FirmVault markdown wiki shadows.
domains: [legal-ops, firmvault]
triggers: [firmvault, case context, activity log, plaintiff file]
capabilities: [read local wiki files, summarize legal matter context]
negative_triggers: [generic coding task]
risk_level: medium            # low | medium | high — TRUSTED FIELD (see merge rule)
profile_allow: [roscoe]
workspace_boost: [firmvault-document-pipeline]
source_path: /path/to/SKILL.md
version_hash: sha256:...
provenance:                    # for third-party / ClawHub skills
  origin: clawhub|local|local-dev
  scan_status: clean|held|unscanned
  signature: present|absent
```

**Card authorship (provenance-aware, per-field merge).** Cards are generated locally by default; maintainer-authored frontmatter is merged over the generated baseline, but the merge rule depends on whether the field is descriptive or security-relevant, and on the skill's origin:

- **Descriptive fields** (`description`, `triggers`, `domains`, `capabilities`, `negative_triggers`) — maintainer frontmatter wins per-field when present.
- **Security-relevant fields** (`risk_level`, `profile_allow`, `provenance`, `scan_status`) are **trusted fields**. They are NOT honored from `clawhub`/third-party-origin frontmatter. The Indexer favors local analysis and ClawHub-signed moderation signals over a skill's self-declaration. Concretely:
  - An untrusted-origin skill defaults to `risk_level: high` until it is both scanned (`scan_status: clean`) and signed (`signature: present`).
  - A self-declared `risk_level` from an untrusted origin may only **raise** that default, never lower it. A third-party `SKILL.md` declaring `risk_level: low` therefore cannot weaken its own gate.
  - Only `local` / maintainer-trusted origins may set `risk_level` freely.

This resolves the input's card-authorship open question — generated-with-maintainer-override for descriptive fields, origin-gated trusted-field handling for security fields.

## 5. Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Indexer
Scans, in precedence order: workspace roots → profile roots → global roots → ClawHub-installed roots. For each `SKILL.md`:
- Parse frontmatter; extract name, description, triggers, domains, capabilities, declared permissions, risk.
- Apply the §4 provenance-aware merge: descriptive fields take maintainer values; security-relevant fields are computed/clamped by the Indexer (trusted-field rule), never self-downgraded by the skill.
- Hash file content (`version_hash`) for incremental invalidation — reindex only changed/added/removed.
- Build the embedding text (below) and store: card, embedding, source path, hash, timestamp.

Embedding text (v1, bounded):
```text
<name>
<description>
Triggers: <triggers>
Domains: <domains>
Capabilities: <capabilities>
Body: <first N bounded chars of skill body>
```

### 5.2 Profile Policy
Each profile has a `skill-policy.yaml`. **Canonical location:** `.openclaw/profiles/<name>/skill-policy.yaml`.
```yaml
profile: roscoe
always_on: [openclaw-core, roscoe-identity, safety-policy]
max_surfaced_default: 8
max_surfaced_hard: 20
allowed_domains: [agent-space, coding, legal-ops, productivity]
blocked_domains: [crypto-trading]
require_confirmation_for: [external-communication, credential-change, payment, publish]
```

Policy ordering is **filter-before-rank** and is normative:
1. Drop `blocked_domains` and deny-listed skills **before** retrieval (they never enter the candidate pool, never get scored, never appear in logs as "almost surfaced").
2. Apply profile allow-list.
3. Apply workspace allow/deny. **Workspace policy is a secondary filter only: it may add boosts or further restrict, but it can never "unblock" a skill denied by the profile master allow-list** (resolves the input's auto-enable-vs-boost open question toward restrict/boost-only).
4. Retrieve + rank the survivors.
5. Apply risk gate (high-risk skills surface only with an explicit trigger/mention match, never on ambient vector similarity alone). The `risk_level` consulted here is the index-time trusted-field value (§4), never re-read from a loaded body.
6. `always_on` skills are **pinned-Loaded infrastructure**: their full bodies are pre-loaded at init (§3), they bypass per-turn retrieval and the per-turn load gate, they are exempt from both the default and hard caps, and they do not displace dynamic surfacing slots — but they remain bound by every §5.7 invariant.

### 5.3 Ambient Retrieval Middleware
Per user message, inputs: message, recent-conversation summary, profile id, workspace path, channel, explicit skill mentions.

Hybrid pipeline:
- Vector: embed query, take `top_k_vector` from the **policy-filtered** index.
- Lexical: BM25 over name/triggers/domains, take `top_k_lexical`.
- **Normalize each score family to `[0,1]` over the retrieved candidate set, before fusion:**
  - vector cosine → `(cos + 1) / 2`;
  - BM25 (unbounded) → min-max over the lexical candidate set.
- **Fuse** by weighted linear combination on the normalized scale: `fused = w_v · norm_vec + w_l · norm_lex`, with `w_v + w_l = 1` (defaults `w_v = 0.6`, `w_l = 0.4`). Dedup near-identical entries by `version_hash` + name similarity.
- Adjust the fused score on this same `[0,1]` scale: `+workspace_boost`, `+exact_trigger_boost`, `+explicit_mention_boost`, `−negative_trigger_penalty`.
- Threshold at `min_score`, truncate to `surface_target`, hard-cap at `surface_max_hard`.

> **Why normalization (not RRF):** both score families are commensurated onto one `[0,1]` similarity scale before fusing, so the additive boosts and the `min_score` floor act on a single, interpretable quantity. A floor on a normalized fused similarity is meaningfully more stable across embedders than a floor on a raw absolute cosine. (Reciprocal Rank Fusion was considered and rejected during convergence — see Resolved Decisions.)

Defaults (tunable per profile):
```yaml
top_k_vector: 20
top_k_lexical: 10
w_v: 0.6                       # vector weight in the normalized fuse
w_l: 0.4                       # lexical weight in the normalized fuse
surface_target: 5
surface_max_default: 8
surface_max_hard: 20
min_score: 0.42                # threshold on the normalized fused score; MiniLM-calibrated (see §11)
explicit_mention_min_score: 0.0   # named skills bypass the floor (still policy-gated)
workspace_boost: 0.08
exact_trigger_boost: 0.12
negative_trigger_penalty: 0.20
```

**Threshold portability requirement:** `min_score: 0.42` is calibrated for the default `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` embedder (§11). Any change of embedding model MUST trigger a re-calibration pass against the evaluation set (§9) to find the new threshold that yields equivalent recall; the floor is documented as model-specific, not a universal constant.

Output: ordered surfaced cards, each with score + reason list.

### 5.4 Deliberate Manifest Search
```ts
skill_manifest_search({ query, profile?, workspace?, includeBlocked? }) → SkillCard[]
skill_load({ skillId, reason }) → SkillBody | PolicyDenied
```
`skill_manifest_search` returns cards only. `includeBlocked: true` may list blocked skills as *visible-but-unloadable* (so the agent can explain to the user why something is unavailable) — it never bypasses the load gate. `skill_load` re-runs policy at load time and returns the body only if allowed; a denied load returns a structured reason, never a partial body.

### 5.5 Explainability & Logs
Every surface and load emits the canonical decision record:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-06-23T15:20:00-04:00",
  "profile": "roscoe", "workspace": "agent-space",
  "userMessageHash": "sha256:...",
  "skillId": "frontend-design",
  "decision": "surfaced",        // surfaced | loaded | blocked | denied
  "score": 0.71,
  "reasons": ["vector_match", "workspace_boost", "domain:frontend"],
  "policy": "allowed"
}
```
Inspectable from CLI (`openclaw skills surfaced --last`) and UI. Logs store the message **hash**, not the message, by default. This record is the single source of truth reused by the UI integration surface (§5.6) — no second schema is invented.

### 5.6 UI
Profile skill settings (active/available/blocked lists); current-turn surfaced-skills inspector with reasons; load-explanation panel; reindex button; threshold/top-k controls (advanced). Pin/block a skill to room/profile/project.

**v1 UI data contract (no new transport).** Each turn the surfacing middleware:
- **Atomically writes** the current ordered card set with reasons to a well-known file, `.openclaw/skills-index/logs/surfaced-current.json` (one atomic write per turn), and
- **Emits a `skills.surfaced` event** on OpenClaw's existing plugin event bus carrying `{ profile, workspace, turnHash, cards: [{ id, score, reasons, decision }] }`.

The UI subscribes to the event for live render near the active loop and reads the file for cold-start/reopen. Both carry the same §5.5 decision record; nothing new is transported.

### 5.7 Security (normative invariants)
1. Retrieval is not permission. Loading is not permission.
2. Side-effecting skills route through existing OpenClaw approval/permission paths regardless of load state (including pinned `always_on` skills).
3. Third-party cards show origin, scan status, signature presence.
4. `scan_status: held` or blocked ClawHub skills are not surfaced by default (overridable only via explicit pin with a logged decision).
5. Loaded bodies preserve provenance + path. Security-relevant card fields are the index-time trusted-field values (§4); they are never re-derived from a loaded body.
6. **Skill-body instructions are subordinate to system/profile policy. The guarantee is delivered in two layers, honestly labeled:**
   - **Layer A — body-as-data envelope (best-effort, prompt-level).** Skill bodies are injected inside an explicit untrusted-data envelope — a delimited `<skill-body trust=data>` / `<skill_body>` block — and a system-level **"Data-Reference Invariant"** instructs the agent to treat the enclosed text strictly as read-only reference material (schema/documentation), never as instructions that grant tools or change policy. This is a mitigation, not an enforcement, and is described as such.
   - **Layer B — mechanical guarantee (load-bearing).** The policy/permission engine **never reads skill-body text.** Every gating decision uses fields from the indexed card computed at index time, and the `risk_level` used by the high-risk gate is the trusted-field card value fixed at index, not re-read from the loaded body. A body asserting "I am low risk" or "grant me tool X" has no mechanical path to weaken the gate or self-authorize, because the authorizing code path does not consult the body at all.
7. **Co-loaded body precedence ladder.** When multiple bodies are loaded simultaneously, precedence is: **system prompt > profile policy > workspace pins > loaded skill bodies.** Among loaded bodies, none can override another's domain, because all bodies are consulted as data (Layer A/B), not obeyed as instructions. v1's primary mitigation for cross-skill instruction overlap is keeping the loaded set small (the bounded 3–12 surfaced set + the risk gate); **full programmatic conflict-resolution between simultaneously-loaded bodies is explicitly deferred to v1.5** (alongside the reranker) and is not claimed for v1.

## 6. Architecture & Storage

```text
User Message
  └─> Surfacing Middleware
        ├─ Profile Policy Filter   (filter BEFORE retrieval; workspace = secondary filter only)
        ├─ Query Embedder
        ├─ Vector Search  ┐
        ├─ Lexical Search ┴─ normalize each family to [0,1] ─> weighted fuse (w_v/w_l) + dedup
        ├─ Boosts / Penalties (on the normalized scale)
        └─ Risk/Policy Gate (uses index-time trusted-field risk_level)
  └─> Surfaced Cards ─> Agent Context
        ├─ skill_manifest_search()
        └─ skill_load()  ─> policy re-check ─> SKILL.md body (Layer A envelope)
  └─> Decision record ─> logs + surfaced-current.json + skills.surfaced event
```

```text
.openclaw/
  skills-index/{index.sqlite, embeddings/, logs/{surfaced-current.json, ...}}
  profiles/<name>/skill-policy.yaml      # canonical policy location
```
Storage: SQLite + a vector extension already shipped by OpenClaw (sqlite-vec / sqlite-vss / LanceDB), falling back to a flat local index. **Decision:** wrap native skill loading as middleware rather than fork it — the plugin owns surfacing, native loading stays the execution primitive `skill_load` calls, and the middleware can intercept/block load requests without forking the core runtime. Resolves the input's "alter vs wrap" open question toward wrap.

## 7. Ranking Roadmap
- **v1:** local small embedder (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), hybrid vector+lexical with normalized weighted fusion, policy-first filter, workspace/profile boosts, no LLM reranker.
- **v1.5:** optional local reranker over top-20; bounded full-body indexing; near-duplicate clustering; **programmatic conflict-resolution between co-loaded skill bodies** (the homogeneous-catalog problem — body text and listwise comparison matter more as the catalog grows).
- **v2:** eval dataset, learned weights, per-profile feedback, registry-scale retrieve-and-rerank.

## 8. MVP & Acceptance

MVP: index local skills; per-profile `skill-policy.yaml` at the canonical path; surface 5–8 cards/turn; `skill_manifest_search` + `skill_load`; decision logging; CLI:
```bash
openclaw skills index
openclaw skills surface "query" --profile roscoe --workspace /path
openclaw skills policy edit roscoe
openclaw skills surfaced --last
```
MVP success ≠ perfect routing. MVP success = prompt-clutter reduction with reliable recovery via manifest search.

**Acceptance criteria**
- 189 active skills → ordinary messages surface ≤ 8 by default.
- A blocked domain never surfaces.
- A workspace boost lifts relevant skills without making them globally active, and a workspace can never unblock a profile-denied skill.
- Naming a skill surfaces it iff policy allows.
- The agent can recover misses via manifest search.
- A policy-blocked skill cannot be loaded (denied load returns reason, no body).
- A third-party skill self-declaring `risk_level: low` cannot lower its gate below the trusted-field default.
- Every surfaced skill carries a human-readable reason.
- Reindex detects changed `SKILL.md` by hash.
- Works offline with local skills.

## 9. Metrics
Avg surfaced/turn; load precision (acceptance); **miss rate** (manifest searches after ambient surfacing — the key health signal); blocked-retrieval count; token reduction vs full list; time-to-first-useful-load.

**Eval ground truth — multi-label "equivalence set."** In a homogeneous catalog the goal is to surface *the right capability*, not one specific file. Ground truth is therefore defined per prompt as the *equivalence set* of skills that satisfy the prompt's domain requirement: a prompt is a **Hit** if **any** skill in its equivalence set is surfaced. This resolves the near-duplicate ambiguity (e.g. three "PDF parser" skills — surfacing any one for a PDF prompt is a success). Eval set: 100 local prompts (direct / indirect / cross-domain / no-skill-needed); track Hit@1/3/5 and false-positive rate against the equivalence-set labels.

## 10. Risks → Mitigations
- Over-filter hides right skill → manifest search + tune `min_score` against eval set.
- Under-filter rebuilds bloat → hard cap + per-profile thresholds.
- Homogeneous skills compete → v1.5 reranker + dedup; equivalence-set eval keeps the metric honest.
- Bad metadata → bad retrieval → maintainer-field merge + reindex; surface low-confidence cards with a "weak match" reason rather than silently dropping.
- Metadata-stuffing / self-downgrading malicious skill → filter-before-rank; trusted-field risk handling (self-declared risk can only raise); scan-status signal; Layer-B mechanical gate.
- Surfaced-vs-approved confusion → UI states (installed/surfaced/loaded/pinned) + retrieval-is-not-permission enforced at the tool boundary.
- Embedder swap silently breaks the floor → mandatory re-calibration pass (§5.3).

## 11. Resolved vs Open

**Resolved in this draft:**
- Wrap (not fork) native loading.
- Cards generated-with-maintainer-override for descriptive fields; origin-gated trusted-field handling for security fields.
- Filter-before-rank ordering; workspace policy is boost/restrict-only (cannot unblock).
- Risk gate requires explicit match for high-risk; `risk_level` is an index-time trusted field.
- Logs store message hash, not body.
- **Score fusion: per-candidate-set normalization + weighted linear fuse (`w_v=0.6/w_l=0.4`), with boosts and the `0.42` floor on the normalized scale.** RRF was considered and rejected (see Resolved Decisions).
- **`always_on` = pinned-Loaded infrastructure** (auto-injected at init, exempt from caps, bound by all §5.7 invariants).
- Body-as-data split into Layer A (best-effort envelope: `<skill_body>` tags + Data-Reference Invariant) and Layer B (mechanical: policy engine never reads body text).
- **Default local embedder: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`** (balance of speed and performance on short metadata strings); the `0.42` floor is its calibrated value, with mandatory re-calibration on any embedder change.
- **Canonical `skill-policy.yaml` location: `.openclaw/profiles/<name>/skill-policy.yaml`.**

**Must close before v1** (the MVP path depends on each; criteria above are not claimed fully testable until both are confirmed):
- (a) Lock and ship the `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` default embedder and validate `0.42` against the eval set (the normalized fuse makes this floor far more embedder-portable than a raw cosine, but it still ships as a calibrated value).
- (b) Confirm the canonical `skill-policy.yaml` path end-to-end against the §8 MVP CLI.

**Deferrable to v1.5:**
- ClawHub provenance-metadata completeness — degrades gracefully (missing fields render as `scan_status: unscanned`, which the conservative risk default already handles).
- Cross-agent native skill-list interaction when OpenClaw launches external agents (Codex/Claude native skill lists) — re-derive surfacing at the agent boundary; not on the MVP path.
- Programmatic conflict-resolution between co-loaded skill bodies (with the reranker).

## 12. Recommendation
Ship as a plugin. Prove the loop locally — index, enforce policy, surface small sets, support manifest search, load on demand, log every decision — measure miss rate and token reduction against the eval set, then fold surfacing into core OpenClaw once the thresholds and UI have earned defaults. The plugin boundary is the feature: skill routing needs tuning before it becomes platform behavior.

Based on thorough exploration of the Gas City codebase and the live lawyer-city deployment, here is the precise execution contract:

### 1. CONCRETE ON-DISK ENTITIES (City/Rig/Agent/Convoy)

#### City Structure
A **city** is a directory rooted at the city path (e.g., `/Users/aaronwhaley/Agent-Corporation/lawyer-city`).

**File paths:**
- `/city.toml` — declarative city configuration (workspace, providers, packs, agents, rigs, formulas v2 settings)
- `/.beads/` — bead store root (Dolt-backed by default)
  - `/.beads/dolt/` — Dolt repository for work persistence
  - `/.beads/formulas/` — symlinks to formula definitions (cached from packs)
  - `/.beads/interactions.jsonl` — routable beads log (append-only)
  - `/.beads/routes.jsonl` — bead-store routing table (rig prefix → relative path mapping)
- `/.gc/` — Gas City controller runtime
  - `/.gc/controller.lock` — flock-based single-controller enforcement
  - `/.gc/controller.sock` — Unix socket for control commands (stop, reload, converge)
  - `/.gc/events.jsonl` — all system events (append-only; observed by humans, orders, agents)
  - `/.gc/runtime/` — session and runtime traces (excluded from config watch to prevent churn)
  - `/.gc/nudges/` — per-session nudge queues
- `/agents/` — agent template definitions (e.g., `/agents/mayor/prompt.template.md`)
- `/formulas/` — city-level formula definitions (can be empty if imported via packs)
- `/orders/` — order trigger definitions
- `/commands/`, `/doctor/`, `/overlays/` — extension directories per pack schema
- `/.claude/`, `/.claude/agents/` — Claude Code integration

#### Rig Structure
A **rig** is an external project (usually a git repo) registered with the city via `gc rig add <path>`.

**In lawyer-city**, rigs are defined in `city.toml` with entries like:
```toml
[[rigs]]
name = "jurytrialsearch"
default_branch = "main"
```

**On disk:** Rigs live elsewhere (not under the city), but each maintains:
- Their own `.beads/` store root (physically separate from city `.beads/`)
- Bead ID prefixes for isolation (e.g., `ju-*` for `jurytrialsearch`)
- Routes in the city's `/.beads/routes.jsonl` (e.g., `{"prefix":"ju","path":"../lawyerincorporated/jurytrialsearch"}`)

**File paths for a rig:**
- `<rig-dir>/.beads/` — rig's independent bead store
- `<rig-dir>/.beads/dolt/` — Dolt repository for this rig's work
- `<rig-dir>/.gc/` — rig-scoped session runtime (minimal; most runtime is city-wide)

#### Agent Structure
An **agent** is pure configuration — a named worker definition in `city.toml` or imported packs.

**Minimal example:**
```toml
[[agent]]
name = "mayor"
provider = "claude"
template = "mayor"  # references agents/mayor/prompt.template.md
max_active_sessions = 1
sling_query = "bd create <bead-id>"  # optional; how to route a bead to this agent
```

**On disk:**
- `agents/<name>/prompt.template.md` — the agent's system prompt
- `agents/<name>/` — optional supporting files for that agent

**Agent identity formats:**
- Bare name: `mayor` (city-scoped)
- Import-qualified: `gc.mayor` (from `gc` import binding)
- Rig-qualified: `jurytrialsearch/mayor` (rig-scoped agent, must be city-scoped if imported)
- Full: `jurytrialsearch/gc.mayor` (rig context + import binding)

#### Convoy Structure
A **convoy** is a container bead (type=convoy) grouping related work.

**On disk:** Conveies are **beads** — one row in the Dolt-backed `.beads/` store, **not** a directory.

**Convoy lifecycle:**
1. Created when work arrives (automatically or via `gc sling ... --no-convoy=false` default)
2. Materializes as a parent bead with `status=open`
3. Contains child beads (dependencies via `needs` edges, not parent-child in the bead sense)
4. Closed when all children close OR manually via `bd close <convoy-id>`

### 2. HOW WORK ARRIVES AT AN AGENT

#### The Work Arrival Flow

**Step 1: Work Entry Points**
Work reaches an agent through three mechanisms:

a) **Sling dispatch** (`gc sling <target> <bead-or-formula>`):
   - Creates a bead with `status=open` in the bead store
   - Routes it to an agent's `sling_query` (e.g., `bd create <bead-id>`)
   - File: `/Users/aaronwhaley/Agent-Corporation/gascity/cmd/gc/cmd_sling.go` (starting ~line 57)

b) **Formula instantiation** (`gc sling <target> <formula> --formula` or `gc formula cook`):
   - Compiles formula steps into a graph
   - Materializes steps as beads in the store
   - Routes root (v1) or ready steps (v2) to agents
   - File: `internal/formula/` (v2 compiler in `internal/graphv2/`)

c) **Orders** (scheduled dispatch):
   - Defined in `orders/` or imported packs
   - Triggered by patrol loop every `patrol_interval` (default 2s)
   - Fire formulas or shell commands on schedule/event/condition
   - File: `/Users/aaronwhaley/Agent-Corporation/gascity/cmd/gc/cmd_supervisor.go`, patrol reconciliation loop

#### What Gets Written: The Bead Store Interface

When work arrives, **a bead is written to `.beads/dolt/`**:
- Accessed via Dolt SQL or the `bd` CLI
- A bead has: `id`, `title`, `status` (open/in_progress/closed), `type` (task/mail/session/convoy), `metadata` dict
- Multiple backends supported: Dolt (default), file-based (`GC_BEADS=file`), in-memory
- Single unified store: city + all rig stores share one Dolt instance per city (routed by bead prefix)

**Query interface** (`internal/beads/query.go`):
```go
type QueryFunc = func(Store, ...BeadQuerier) ([]Bead, error)
```

Beads are **not** files on disk — they are **rows in a versioned database** that survives agent crashes.

#### Work Queue Mechanism: The Reconciliation Controller

The **controller** loop runs continuously (launched by `gc start` or `gc supervisor run`).

**File:** `/Users/aaronwhaley/Agent-Corporation/gascity/cmd/gc/controller.go` (reconciliation core)

**What it does:**
1. **Locks the city:** acquires `/.gc/controller.lock` with flock — only one controller per city
2. **Listens for commands:** opens Unix socket at `/.gc/controller.sock` for external commands (stop, reload, etc.)
3. **Runs convergence loop:** bounded iterative refinement that:
   - Reads desired state (agents, formulas, orders from city config)
   - Reads actual state (live sessions, beads, convoy status from store + events)
   - **Dispatches ready work to agents** — this is the core reconciliation
   - Manages session pools (start/stop/resize pools per agent's `scale_check` query)
   - Routes beads to agents via their `sling_query`
   - Handles retries, waits, and order triggers
4. **Emits events:** writes to `/.gc/events.jsonl` for humans and agent observers to watch

#### Agent Session Spawning

When a bead is ready and the agent has capacity:

**File:** `cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_start.go`, `cmd/gc/session_reconciler_fork_launch.go`

**What happens:**
1. Controller reads bead status = `open` from store
2. Checks agent pool capacity (current sessions < `max_active_sessions`)
3. **Constructs a runtime.Config:**
   ```go
   type Config struct {
       Command      string            // e.g., "claude --resume <session-id>"
       Env          map[string]string // GC_CITY, GC_RIG, GC_BEAD_ID, etc.
       Dir          string            // working directory
       Provider     string            // e.g., "claude" or "tmux"
   }
   ```
4. **Spawns the worker process:**
   - For Claude provider: `claude --resume <session-uuid>` (headless Claude Code session)
   - For tmux provider: runs in a named tmux session
   - For exec/ACP/K8s: provider-specific launch
   - **The spawned process inherits environment with `GC_BEAD_ID=<id>`** — this is the signal for what to work on

5. **Session becomes a bead too:**
   - A `type=session` bead is created with `status=open`
   - Agent reads this bead to know it's assigned work
   - Session metadata tracks current bead, state, restart count

**Key environment variables passed to worker:**
- `GC_CITY` — city root path
- `GC_RIG` — if rig-scoped, the rig name
- `GC_BEAD_ID` — the work item ID the agent should pick up
- `GC_MODEL` — LLM model override
- `GC_SESSION_ID` — unique session identifier

**Minimal worker command pattern:**
```
claude --resume <session-id> [--model <model>] [other-flags]
```

### 3. BEADS INTEGRATION: Work Items → BD Issues → Reconciliation

#### Bead ↔ BD Issue Mapping

**Beads** (Gas City's work items) and **BD issues** (Beads CLI representation) are **the same thing — different access surfaces**.

- Beads live in `.beads/dolt/` (Dolt-backed)
- `bd` is a CLI wrapper exposing the store as git-like commands
- `bd create "title"` → creates a bead
- `bd show <id>` → reads a bead's full state
- `bd close <id>` → marks bead as closed

**File:** `internal/beads/bdstore.go`, `internal/beads/native_dolt_store.go` (store implementation)

#### Reconciliation: The Convergence Handler

The convergiliation controller calls `convergence.Handle()` which:

**File:** `internal/convergence/reconcile.go`, `internal/convergence/handler.go`

1. **Reads ready beads:** queries beads with `status=open` and no blocking dependencies (`needs` all closed)
2. **Routes each to an agent:** calls agent's `sling_query` or built-in dispatch
3. **Tracks session state:**
   - Each session is a bead that tracks `current_bead_id` in metadata
   - When session crashes, that metadata survives → next session picks up the same bead
4. **Drains convoys:** for multi-step formula work, orchestrates fan-out across available agents
5. **Handles formulas v2 graphs:**
   - Formula v2 materializes as a flat bead graph (not nested parent-child)
   - Each step is independently routable via `gc.run_target` metadata
   - Graph is driven by blocking-dependency edges (`needs`)
   - Workflow root waits for a finalize step to mark completion

#### Formula v2 Compilation → Beads

**File:** `internal/graphv2/` (formula compiler), `internal/formula/` (instantiation)

Formula TOML like:
```toml
[requires]
formula_compiler = ">=2.0.0"

[[step]]
id = "decompose"
phase = "open"
gc.run_target = "mayor"

[[step]]
id = "build"
needs = ["decompose"]
gc.run_target = "builder"
```

Compiles to:
1. A **workflow root bead** (`type=convoy`, status=open, marking the whole run)
2. **Step beads** for each step (one row per step in `.beads/dolt`)
3. **Blocking edges** stored as `needs` metadata (bead won't become ready until blockers close)
4. **A finalize bead** that the root waits on

### 4. EXTERNAL ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (Roscoe/Omnigent as Waypoint Executor)

For Roscoe (in Omnigent) to use Gas City as its execution backend via Waypoint:

#### Required CLI Commands

**a) Create a city for a project:**
```bash
gc init <city-path>
cd <city-path>
gc start  # daemon startup
```

**b) Register a rig (project repo):**
```bash
gc rig add <project-path> [--name <rig-name>]
```
Creates an entry in `city.toml [[rigs]]` and initializes `.beads/` in the rig.

**c) Define worker agents:**
In `pack.toml` or `city.toml`, add agent blocks:
```toml
[[agent]]
name = "builder"
provider = "claude"
template = "builder"
max_active_sessions = 4
sling_query = "bd create <bead-id>"
```

**d) Dispatch a task:**
```bash
gc sling <rig>/<agent> <description>
# or
gc sling <rig>/<agent> <formula-name> --formula
```

Returns a bead ID and optionally a convoy ID.

**e) Monitor completion:**
```bash
gc events --follow  # stream all events
bd show <bead-id>    # check a specific bead status
```

**f) Collect results:**
Once bead is `closed`:
- Read bead metadata (contains conversation history, outputs)
- Artifacts written by agent are in git commits (agent makes commits in the rig repo)
- Mail beads carry inter-agent messages

**g) Scale agents:**
The controller auto-scales per agent's `scale_check` query. Manually adjust:
```bash
# In city.toml, change an agent's max_active_sessions, then:

```

#### HTTP API (Alternative to CLI)

**File:** `internal/api/` — Gas City exposes an HTTP API via socket/loopback.

Endpoints:
- `POST /sling` — dispatch work
- `GET /beads/<id>` — read bead state
- `GET /events` — subscribe to event stream (websocket)
- `POST /formula/cook` — instantiate without routing
- `POST /order/fire` — manually trigger an order

**Minimal librarification:** Gas City is **primarily operator CLI tooling**, but the HTTP API surface is stable enough for library embedding. Waypoint would:
1. Launch a city daemon: `gc start --socket <path>`
2. Call HTTP endpoints to dispatch/monitor
3. Poll events for completion
4. Read final beads to collect results

### 5. RESULTS/ARTIFACTS FLOW BACK

#### Artifact Persistence Mechanisms

**a) Bead Metadata:**
- Agent writes metadata to its current session bead via `bd edit` or Gas City SDK
- Survives session crash (stored in `.beads/dolt`)
- Read back via `bd show <bead-id>`

**b) Git Commits (Default):**
- Agent runs `git commit` in the rig directory
- Commits are pushed if configured
- External systems read commit history to get results
- **Closure signal:** Agent closes its assigned bead via `bd close <bead-id>` when done

**c) Mail Beads (Inter-Agent Communication):**
- One agent sends: `bd mail <recipient-agent> "message" <source-bead-id>`
- Creates a `type=mail` bead with recipient's agent name in metadata
- Recipient agent reads: `bd list --type mail --recipient <name>`
- Used for hand-offs between agents

**d) Convoy Closure:**
- Parent convoy (container bead) stays open until all children close
- When all children are `closed`, convoy can auto-close or stay open for audit
- v2 finalize step marks the end of a workflow

#### Closure/Completion Signal

**In Gas City, "completion" means:**
1. Bead status transitions from `open` → `in_progress` → `closed`
2. Agent explicitly calls `bd close <bead-id>` when done
3. Gas City events fire: `{"type":"bead.closed","subject":"<bead-id>"}`
4. Orchestrator marks that step ready and moves to dependents

**File:** `internal/beads/closeorder/` — close protocol and ordering

#### Collecting Results in Waypoint

Waypoint (via Roscoe) would:
1. **Dispatch:** `gc sling <rig>/<agent> <input>`  → bead ID
2. **Monitor:** `gc events --follow | grep "bead.closed.*<bead-id>"`
3. **Collect:** `bd show <bead-id>` → full metadata + conversation history
4. **Commit:** Read git log from rig for artifacts
5. **Clean up:** Dispatch optional cleanup formula (core pack includes cleanup order)

### 6. FRANK ASSESSMENT: Runnable as Library vs. CLI Tooling

#### Gas City's Nature
Gas City is **fundamentally operator-driven CLI tooling with optional library affordances**.

**Strong CLI-first signals:**
- City root + `.gc/` + `.beads/` are filesystem-rooted, not in-process
- Controller is a daemon process (not in-library), communicates via Unix socket + events.jsonl
- Configuration is filesystem-based (TOML files), not structs
- Session spawning is process-level (via tmux/subprocess/K8s provider, not in-process threads)
- Session recovery relies on flock + socket handshakes, not in-memory state

#### Can It Be a Daemon Under Another App?

**Yes, with limitations:**
1. **Start as a daemon:** `gc start --socket <path>` launches controller as background process
2. **HTTP API:** Use REST/WebSocket instead of CLI
3. **Multi-city support:** Machine-wide supervisor (`gc supervisor run`) can manage multiple cities simultaneously

**But not truly "librarified":**
- Controller is always a separate process (can't run in parent app's thread)
- Configuration lives on disk (can't be in-memory structs)
- Session spawning happens out-of-process (provider launches independent `claude` / tmux / K8s jobs)

#### Minimal Slice for Waypoint as Executor

**What Waypoint needs from Gas City:**
1. **Bead store abstraction** (`internal/beads/`) — this IS libraryfiable
   - Swap backend: Dolt ↔ file ↔ in-memory
   - Query beads, update status, read/write metadata
   
2. **Dispatch logic** (`internal/sling/`, `internal/dispatch/`) — this IS libraryfiable
   - Take a bead + agent → emit routing command
   - Handle retry/gating logic

3. **Session lifecycle** (`internal/session/`, `internal/runtime/`) — partially libraryfiable
   - Spawn provider sessions (Claude CLI, tmux, K8s)
   - Track session state
   - Adopt orphaned sessions on restart

4. **Formula compilation** (`internal/graphv2/`) — fully libraryfiable
   - Parse formula TOML
   - Compile to DAG
   - Materialize to beads

5. **Convergence/reconciliation** (`internal/convergence/`) — NOT libraryfiable
   - Requires city daemon, controller loop, event broadcast
   - Intrinsically operation-loop machinery

#### Recommended Integration Pattern for Waypoint

**Option A: Use Gas City as External Daemon**
- Waypoint spawns `gc supervisor run` process at startup
- Calls HTTP API to dispatch/monitor
- This is the intended integration model — keeps concerns separate
- Works for both local CLI and cloud deployment

**Option B: Embed Bead Store + Dispatch, Use External Providers**
- Import `internal/beads/` as library
- Embed dispatch logic
- Keep controller/reconciliation as external daemon
- Waypoint owns formula and session lifecycle
- This is a partial embedding — saves learning Gas City's daemon model but requires more Waypoint-side coordination

**Option C: Full Embedding (Not Recommended)**
- Embed everything
- Still need external `claude --resume` process for actual agent work
- Still need `.gc/` filesystem root for events/state
- Gains little (most complexity stays in the daemon loop)
- Adds technical debt (tightly coupling codebases)

**Recommended: Option A** — treat Gas City as a service tier, use HTTP API. Keeps clean separation.

### 3. THE CASE TEMPLATE & VAULT LAYOUT: Clean but partially migrated

**The template structure** (`skills.tools.workflows/case_template/blank-personal-injury-case/`):
```
_case-slug.md               (frontmatter + body sections)
accident/                   (accident, police-report, liability)
activity/                   (activity log entries + metadata)
client/                     (intake, contracts, authorizations, contactability, check-ins)
contacts/                   (per-provider, per-adjuster, per-defendant stubs)
demand/                     (draft, exhibits, sent-to)
documents/                  (buckets: insurance/, medical/, legal/, evidence/, correspondence/, communications/, _extractions/)
insurance/                  (per-carrier BI/PIP/UIM claim files with offer tracking)
liens/                      (per-creditor lien stubs)
litigation/                 (complaint, service, discovery, mediation, disposition)
medical-providers/          (provider contact stubs — actually go under contacts/)
negotiation/                (offer log, counter history, settlement tracking)
settlement/                 (statement, authorization, release, distribution)
tickle.md                   (manual reminders / follow-ups)
workflow-log/               (deprecated, migrated to activity/)
```

**Divergence from Waypoint (the other repo's quest model):**

Waypoint treats a case as a **quest** with **milestones** → **phases** → **plans** → **tasks** → **recipe executions**. The FirmVault model is flatter:

| Concept | Waypoint | FirmVault |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| Top-level unit | Quest (one per case) | Case folder + frontmatter status |
| Sequencing | Workflow DAG (quests.yaml) + Plan dependency graph | PHASE_DAG.yaml core_phases + parallel_tracks |
| Work definition | Recipe (reusable agent skill) + Plan (instance) | Task template (YAML) + Skill (markdown+references) |
| State storage | Engine-host database + workspace files | Git-tracked case frontmatter `landmarks:` map |
| Execution dispatch | Waypoint CLI / engine-host API | GitHub Issues (planned, not live) or cron + subprocess |
| Review gates | `gate: { required: true, kind: ... }` nodes in Plan | `review: true` flag in task template (human comment gate) |
| Audit trail | Waypoint event log (internal) | Git commits (diffable, permanent) |

**The predicted integration breakage:**
- **Slug/ID parity:** FirmVault uses `cases/<case-slug>/` with strict slug rules (lowercase, no apostrophes). Waypoint quests use `quest_id` (opaque UUIDs or stable strings). A quest's first-class `name` field ("Jordan Brown") is human-readable but is *not* the filesystem anchor. If a quest is promoted to Waypoint and later referenced as `[slug]`, the mapping must be externally maintained.
- **Landmark storage mismatch:** FirmVault owns landmarks in case-file frontmatter (`landmarks: { client_info_received: true, ... }`). Waypoint's engine-host stores plan/phase/milestone progress in its database + workspace files. Syncing these after a quest lands is non-trivial; either Waypoint polls the vault, or the vault polls Waypoint, or a bridge service maintains a live mapping.
- **Parallel tracks vs sub-quests:** FirmVault's parallel tracks (PIP, liens, SOL, client contact, litigation) are designed to coexist without blocking the main phase sequence. Waypoint's model treats sub-quests as branching off the main flow. A litigation track that runs *alongside* demand/negotiation (not instead of) would need to be represented as either a parallel Plan within a single Quest or as an external Quest with cross-quest dependencies — neither is elegant in the current schema.
- **Document/ledger path collision:** Waypoint's folder-host packages allow arbitrary nested structure. FirmVault's DATA_CONTRACT.md v4 mandates a specific bucket layout for documents. If a quest creates `[case-folder]/research/demand-strategy.md`, it sits outside the v4 contract. Either the quest is constrained to the buckets, or the vault contract relaxes and loses enforcement.

### 7. THE PREDICTED INTEGRATION BREAKAGE (vs Waypoint quest model)

| Issue | Severity | How it manifests |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| **Slug/ID mismatch** | High | FirmVault cases are `cases/<slug>/` (git-based). Waypoint quests use `quest_id` (opaque). Cross-referencing requires an external mapping. A case migrated to Waypoint becomes a quest with an auto-generated ID; syncing landmarks back to the vault requires bidirectional polling or a dedicated bridge. |
| **Landmark storage divergence** | High | FirmVault stores landmarks in YAML frontmatter. Waypoint's engine-host stores phase/plan progress in database. If a quest is created *from* a FirmVault case, the quest's initial state must be bootstrapped from the case file. If the quest is updated in Waypoint, the case file must be re-synced — or they drift. |
| **Parallel tracks vs sub-quests** | Medium | FirmVault's litigation/PIP/lien tracks run alongside the main phase. Waypoint's model treats branches as alternative Quests or sub-Plans. A litigation track that *doesn't* exit to settlement (stays running while negotiation continues) is awkward to model in Quest semantics. Either Waypoint's model needs to be extended, or FirmVault's parallel tracks need to be flattened into branching paths. |
| **Document bucket enforcement** | Medium | DATA_CONTRACT.md v4 specifies `documents/{insurance,medical,legal,evidence,correspondence,communications,_extractions}/`. Waypoint quests may create artifacts outside these buckets. Either the quest is constrained (and documentation updated), or the vault contract is relaxed (and CI guard is disabled). |
| **Skill vs Recipe mapping** | Low | FirmVault's SKILL.md files are agent-facing markdown. Waypoint recipes are authoring proposals + execution plans. A skill can be wrapped as a recipe, but the *inputs*, *preconditions*, and *success checks* need explicit mapping. Not blocking, but requires translation layer. |
| **Review gate SLA drift** | Low | FirmVault task templates have `priority: high|normal|low` but no formal SLA fields. Waypoint gates have `required: true` but no SLA. If both systems are live, review bottlenecks in one may not be visible to the other. |

**Bottom line:** The two systems are *conceptually compatible* (both are state machines with landmarks and tasks) but *architecturally divergent* (storage, ID scheme, execution model). Merging them requires a bridge service or a complete re-scaffolding of one to adopt the other's data model.

### 8. WHERE THIS MOST DISAGREES WITH MARKDOWN+MASKING+GIT-REVIEW SUBSTRATE

FirmVault's thesis is: **"The firm as a code repo."** Real insight. But there are friction points:

1. **PII remains partially visible** — case names are slug-ified but still human-readable. True masking would use opaque IDs (uuid-xxx) and keep a separate PII mapping. The current tradeoff (readable slugs, masked document content) is pragmatic but not belt-and-suspenders.

2. **No enforce-able schema versioning in git diffs** — A PR can add a case file with `schema_version: 2` (v3 shape) and it won't fail CI until the contract-guard script runs. The guard is in `.github/workflows/` but was only added 2026-07-02. Before that, drift was silent.

3. **Landmarks as frontmatter booleans are coarse** — FirmVault uses `landmarks: { client_info_received: true }`. This works but doesn't capture *when* the landmark was satisfied or *by whom*. Activity logs capture timestamps, but landmark satisfaction is implicit. If you need to know "who approved demand?", you have to grep the activity log for a matching entry. This is solvable (add `satisfied_by`, `satisfied_date` to each landmark), but it's currently coarse.

4. **Masking discipline relies on convention, not code** — `{{client_ssn}}` is a placeholder, but nothing prevents a skill from writing the raw value. The PII protection relies on agents following the convention + manual review. A stronger model would use a secrets engine (SOPS + age, or GitHub Secrets, or AWS Secrets Manager) to inject at render time.

5. **No built-in conflict detection** — Two agents could create tasks on the same case simultaneously without knowing it. Git prevents *commits* from colliding (merge conflicts), but in-flight work is not coordinated. This is solvable (task claims, leases, work-tree locks) but not currently implemented.

**The repo is a rigorous contract layer with a half-wired automation engine.**

It is:
- **Well-designed:** PHASE_DAG is a real state machine, DATA_CONTRACT is explicit, skills are modernized, task templates are comprehensive.

- **Integrated with Waypoint:** Conceptually compatible; architecturally divergent. Bridge required.

The contract is durable; the execution layer is scaffolded and waiting for a runtime decision (which of the 5 candidate Arch 1–5 approaches in `experiments/` to actually run).

**Risk if used today:** Feeding a case into this vault works fine (it lands in git, structure is enforced). Running a case *through* the workflow (materializer→worker→review loop) would surface missing pieces: no task dispatch, no worker runtime, no integration with Waypoint if that's where the UI lives.
